m.aarti.tek: Ambā, you are Jagadambā, the mother of the world, you are Kālī; victory to you, Durgā, who bears the skull-bowl. Bhāratī (Sarasvatī) sings your glories alone; O Mother, we all wave the lamps of your āratī.
m.aarti.pad1: Mother, heavy trouble has fallen on your devotees. Fall upon the host of demons, Mother, riding your lion. Mightier than hundreds of lions, eight-armed, you take away the sorrow of the sorrowing.
m.aarti.pad2: In this world the bond between mother and son is pure indeed. Unworthy sons have been heard of, but never an unworthy mother. You show compassion to all, you rain down nectar, and you take away the sorrow of the sorrowing.
m.aarti.pad3: We do not ask for wealth and riches, neither silver nor gold. We ask only for one small corner of your heart. You set right what has gone wrong for everyone, you protect honour, and you uphold the virtue of faithful women.
